title: SEER: Super-Optimization Explorer for High-Level Synthesis using E-graph Rewriting
problem: High-level synthesis tools produce hardware designs with significant performance gaps compared to manual implementations because HLS programs must adhere to hardware design principles. Current HLS approaches cannot effectively explore the optimization space to discover superior program transformations that yield better hardware designs.
motivation: Closing the performance gap between HLS-generated and manually-designed hardware is essential for making hardware design more accessible and efficient.
method: SEER uses e-graph rewriting to systematically explore semantically equivalent program transformations for HLS inputs. The approach constructs equivalence graphs representing different program variants and applies rewriting rules to discover optimization opportunities. It selects optimal designs from the explored space based on hardware synthesis quality metrics.
key_novelty: Using e-graph rewriting to systematically explore program transformation space and discover hardware-efficient program variants for high-level synthesis.
contributions: E-graph rewriting framework tailored for HLS program optimization
Super-optimization explorer methodology for searching program transformation space
Approach to reduce performance gap between HLS-generated and manual hardware designs
limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: E-graph based super-optimization for high-level synthesis
